verification_justification: Corrects two independently-reviewed critical blockers on an existing open PR (docs/design-contract ancestry, and three dispatchable execution-graph.md rows with no Codex-side implementation mapping). No new deployed/outward surface is introduced by the fix itself — it removes rows and merges a doc commit — so no verification_level-2 predicate fires. Not verification_level 0: the two blockers were freshly found by an independent review and have no pre-existing test/verify-criterion covering them (the exec_bit_invariant test only started covering the 2 target scripts because this fix registers them). Strongest surface (rule 6): the goal state is 'does this branch's own history and live-parsed contract satisfy what the review demanded' — git ancestry checks and a live call into codex/runtime/graph.py's own prepare_implementations are the direct exercise of that surface, not a substitute for it.

evals.assert: codex/runtime/graph.py's prepare_implementations() called against this branch's execution-graph.md, in live mode with an empty implementations config and 2 templated work units, produces the identical set of 'missing implementation mapping' errors as the same call against origin/main's execution-graph.md — i.e. this PR introduces zero new dispatch regressions to the live Codex graph runtime.

REPO=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); cd "$REPO"; MAIN_DOC=$(mktemp); git show origin/main:skills/agentic-loop/execution-graph.md > "$MAIN_DOC" 2>/dev/null || git show main:skills/agentic-loop/execution-graph.md > "$MAIN_DOC"; python3 - "$MAIN_DOC" "$REPO/skills/agentic-loop/execution-graph.md" "$REPO/codex" <<'PYEOF'
import sys
from pathlib import Path
main_doc, new_doc, codex_dir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
sys.path.insert(0, codex_dir)
from runtime import graph
def missing(path):
    g = graph.build_graph(contract_path=Path(path), work_units=['a', 'b'])
    _, errors = graph.prepare_implementations(g, {'mode': 'live', 'nodes': {}, 'gates': {}})
    return sorted(e for e in errors if 'missing implementation mapping' in e)
m, n = missing(main_doc), missing(new_doc)
if m != n:
    print('DIFF main-only:', sorted(set(m) - set(n)))
    print('DIFF new-only:', sorted(set(n) - set(m)))
    sys.exit(1)
sys.exit(0)
PYEOF
rc=$?; unlink "$MAIN_DOC"; exit $rc

amendments.why: Grading against final PR head 826e77790a1517a2dd2a2cdd7ee362d1d5294896 (git log/diff confirmed the only commit between the file's frozen_sha d4b75395 and this head is the evals.json file's own creation commit — no code changed, so the frozen assertions/cmds remained valid). During grading, F3 and F4's negative_control scripts were found to be non-discriminating and were repaired in place; both repairs are disclosed here per the freeze-before-build escape-hatch convention (verification_justification/amendment disclosure), not silently rewritten.
amendments.change: negative_control repaired: the frozen version appended the injected `Zextra-staged-node[i]` row after skills/agentic-loop/execution-graph.md's markdown table ends (past load_contract()'s blank-line break in codex/runtime/graph.py), so the row was never parsed and the mutation was inert — the recorded pass came from m == n trivially holding, not from a real comparison. Repaired version inserts the row inside the table (before its last real row) so build_graph() actually parses it, and re-derives the comparison: the injected node now genuinely appears as a new missing-implementation-mapping entry. Verified independently at grading time: re-running the ORIGINAL frozen negative_control's core comparison (with the row still appended at EOF) still shows main-missing == new-missing (equal: True), proving the original control never discriminated on any run, including the one that produced its recorded smoke evidence.

amendments.why: Same grading pass as the F3 amendment above.
amendments.change: negative_control repaired: the frozen version copied the mutated hooks/scripts/tests/exec_bit_invariant.test.sh to a flat mktemp path outside the repo tree (e.g. /var/folders/.../T/tmp.XXXX). That script derives its own REPO_ROOT from `$(dirname "$0")/../../..`, so run from /tmp it resolved to /var/folders instead of the repo, and every `git ls-files` call inside it failed with 'fatal: not a git repository' — producing FAIL lines for the entire manifest (an unrelated environmental failure) while never emitting or checking for the specific parallel_review_join.sh FAIL line the control was meant to prove. Verified independently at grading time: grepping the original control's captured output for 'parallel_review_join' returns zero matches. Repaired version copies the mutated script to a same-relative-depth location inside hooks/scripts/tests/ (untracked, excluded from the test's own manifest scan by its `grep -v '/tests/'` filter, cleaned up on every path) so REPO_ROOT resolves correctly, and asserts on the actual FAIL line for the removed manifest entry.
